info: May be repeated in the same or separate terms to a maximum of 6 hours if topics vary. Prerequisite: SPAN 228 or consent of instructor.

sections.sectionText: TOPIC TITLE: Scary stories: The strange, the monstrous, and the supernatural in Spanish and Latin American texts. It’s well known that scary stories help us process deep human fears and anxieties, but they also offer a reflection of larger cultural anxieties connected to social instability. We’ll examine stories and films from a variety of historical periods and Spanish-speaking regions, allowing ourselves to experience them both emotionally and intellectually.

subject: SPAN
title: History of the Spanish Language
info: 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. Prerequisite: SPAN 252 or equivalent introduction to Spanish or General Linguistics or consent of instructor.

sections.sectionText: Study of the historical evolution of the Spanish language, from its origins in Latin to its spread and development in Spain and Latin America, considering also the influence of other languages on Spanish. Both internal history (changes in phonology, morphology, syntax and lexicon) and external history are examined. Taught in Spanish. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. Prerequisite: SPAN 252 or equivalent introduction to Spanish or General Linguistics or consent of instructor.

sections.sectionText: TOPIC TITLE: Applied Sociolinguistics COURSE DESCRIPTION: This graduate seminar is dedicated to using sociolinguistics to make interdisciplinary connections via applied research. Readings will include topics related to linguistic variation and perceptual dialectology, as well as work that applies sociolinguistic concepts to contexts such as healthcare, risk communication, business, education, artificial intelligence, and law. Students should have graduate standing and experience with sociolinguistics or seek permission of instructor. Taught in English.
